When the RX rings are created they are also populated with buffers so
that packets can be received. Usually these are kernel buffers
for AF_XDP in zero-copy mode
column2: these are user-space buffers and in this

column1: case the application might not have sent down any buffers to the
driver at this point. And if no buffers are allocated at ring creation
time
column2: no packets can be received and no interrupts will be generated so

column1: the NAPI poll function that allocates buffers to the rings will never
get executed.
To rectify this
column2: we kick the NAPI context of any queue with an

column1: attached AF_XDP zero-copy socket in two places in the code. Once after
an XDP program has loaded and once after the umem is registered.  This
take care of both cases: XDP program gets loaded first then AF_XDP
socket is created
then XDP program is loaded.
